label: Delimiter step, boosted when f/o/j/z are in the sequence
explanation: Mostly a <DEL>-step unit. The delimiter step holds 71% of activation mass (active on 37% of delimiter steps, 7.5x lift) and includes all of the top activations. Firing at the delimiter is more likely when the original sequence contains f, o, j or z (precision 0.37 -> 0.52). The remaining ~27% of mass is weaker firing in the copy phase, mainly on the early outputs (recall_idx 2 especially) when the NEXT output is f/o/j/z (next_out f 5.3x, o 4.8x, j 4.7x, z 4.2x). It almost never fires during the original phase (2% of mass, none at t<2) or on the last few copy steps. The delimiter condition alone gets F1 0.45 / mass recall 0.71; adding the token-set condition gets F1 0.50. Which delimiter steps fire, and how strongly, is not fully captured.
